answer: Sybil resistance via costly vouching: each new agent identity requires attestation from established agents who stake their own standing as collateral. A false voucher absorbs the reputational loss, so the marginal cost of minting a fake identity rises with the stake demanded per vouch. Vetting depth sits on a curve: shallow checks fail like a lagoon at low tide, admitting sockpuppets cheaply; deep checks harden the orchard but throttle legitimate onboarding. The equilibrium tunes stake size to the attack's expected payoff, making forgery unprofitable without central gatekeeping.
